title: [Bug 3.3.1.3] AAPSclient does not fetch data from NS
body:
Happens really frequently (several times a day) : suddenly AAPSClient stops receiving data from NS. If I hit "deliver now", I receive the data at once. I have tried with or without websockets with same result.

It started happening on 3.3.1.3 (my previous version was 3.3.1.0). My phone has proper internet access, because every time I see the last value displayed correctly on xdrip.

[AndroidAPS.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18606533/AndroidAPS.log)

It can be seen in this log several time during the day, from : 
08:03 to 08:21, 
08:49 to 09:04,
09:32 to 09:51,
14:17 to 14:35,
14:38 to 15:02,
15:03 to 15:47,
15:48 to 16:30, 
16:59 to 17:15,
17,43 to 17:54.

comments.body:
I'm guessing you are using NSClientv3? 

Could you try on your AAPSClient, go to maintenance and reset DB. Exit app. And then do a full sync. And see if you experience it again?
Yes NS v3. Thanks for the suggestion, I've tried that and will update here.
Unfortunately it didn't solve the issue.
I am with the same issue. Same version.
Log is strange. Like AAPS is running twice. I'd restart AAPS or phone

The issue was solved on my end after a factory reset of my phone (for another reason, I didn't expect it would solve this).
I suspect that it could be due to the synchronization to the time server disabled on my phone, and being a few minutes off, but I have not verified that.
I fixed deactivating nightscout cloud upload in the xdrip+ application.

Same here. When using NSClientV3 the glucose data from nightscout is not received. When switching back to NSClientV1 then it works again. I updated to 3.3.1.3 a few hours ago and used 3.3.1.0 for several weeks where the same occured. I tried to switch to NSV3 since the battery drain of NSV1 seems to be very high. At least i could not figure out any other app that could be responsible for this battery draining.

What I have done so far to make NSV3 work:
- close AAPS completely and restart it
- clear the database in maintenance
- reset the database in maintenance
- checked time settings in phone settings (is set to automatic)
- reboot the phone

the phone is a pixel 6 from google

I set "nightscout client bz" as datasaource for glucose values. this works with NSV1 but not with NSV3. At the statuspage of NSV3 i can see that there are a lot of entries which start with "RCV" so I think the connection works well, but it really doesn't receive the glucose values.

If you don't receive data using v3 it only does mean it is not uploaded using v3.
This is directly against best practice to let only AAPS upload to NS
Perfect, thank you so much :) I just had to update Juggluco to send it using v3 (declared as test in the app, but working) and now NSV3 works. Great 👍

Still not best practice
Proper way is Jugguco -> AAPS -> NS

I looked for that possibility, but could not find it. So I stuck with reading the glucose values from nightscout. What have I to configure in aaps to read the glucose values from juggluco?

I found out, how to do it. I had to enable the option "xdrip Broadcast" in Juggluco and set the glucose source in AAPS to xDrip+. The AAPS has also to be configured to save glucose values to nightscout. 

Thanks Milos for pointing me in the right direction 👍
